messages.author: 7c2e44f7a6b9ca54
messages.subject: worldmap question
parts:
Hi,

can someone point me to an easy reference text on how I plot a data
frame with two columns, one being the two letter ISO code for
countries and the other an integer (number of observations) so that
it shows as a color map (something like 1-10, 11-100, 101-1000,
1001-100000, > 100000 (with the country missing meaning 0
observation, ie no color))?

The country names in map_date("world") are not exactly the ones in the
ISO code list, which I have to use...

greetings, el

messages.author: 4e979d95e92a2b9e
messages.subject: Re: worldmap question
parts:
Does page 4 in the rworldmap vignette have what you need:
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rworldmap/vignettes/rworldmap.pdf
joinCountryData2Map has joinCode values for ISO2, ISO3, and others.

Tom 2

messages.author: 4e979d95e92a2b9e
messages.subject: Re: worldmap question
parts:
Assuming that the "NA" to NA is in the dataframe and not the map, and that your csv file doesn't have any actually missing values that also use 'NA' as their missing value indicator (instead of just 2 consecutive commas), something like:
isoqueries <- read.csv("qpc.csv",na.strings="")
should work.  I tend to also use as.is=TRUE to prevent conversion of strings to factors, as I almost always do something with the strings before creating factors.  Look at the documentation for
?read.csv

Re the NA for Nambia, I have encountered the exact same problem.

Look at read.table(). There is an argument to identify how missing data are coded in your file. The default is na.strings = "NA",

-Phil
